briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the Climate Briefing for November 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Stalled International Climate Negotiations and the Deprioritization of the Climate Crisis
sections.content: As the COP31 climate summit concluded without reaching a final agreement, the conference president defended the summit's outcome while strongly criticizing the European Union (EU) [15]. Alongside the summit's collapse, analyses revealed that global temperatures exceeded 2 degrees Celsius over a recent six-day period, while flood-ravaged Nepal faces the persistent gap in international climate solidarity [23, 24]. Furthermore, the urgency of climate action is being pushed down the international agenda amid ongoing wars and cost-of-living pressures, and the Conservative Party of British Columbia (BC) in Canada has officially abandoned its climate policy commitments [17, 25].

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Global Warming and Warnings of Water and Urban Crises
sections.content: The United Nations released a pessimistic outlook warning that global warming could surge to 2.8 degrees Celsius under current policies [5]. Extreme heatwaves are already driving global freshwater resources to record lows, and water rates have surged in the Portland area of the United States due to climate change impacts [6, 13]. Additionally, concerns have been raised that climate change could expose subsea internet cables to damage from fishing activities, while over 7 million residents in coastal megacities across Africa are projected to face flood risks by 2050 [18, 29].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Agriculture Shaken by Climate Change and Threats to Native Ecosystems
sections.content: Across South Korea's agricultural sector, unpredictable heatwaves and torrential downpours are causing crop losses to snowball, wiping out entire annual harvests in some cases [2]. The fallout from climate change is even reshaping traditional rice planting calendars, prompting the central region to delay planting while the southern region moves it forward [1, 3, 21]. Meanwhile, aquatic ecosystems have suffered severe blows, sparking concerns that the habitat of the 'gaksibungeo' (Korean rose bitterling)—a native fish species that lays its eggs inside freshwater bivalves—could shrink by up to 90% due to climate change [4].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Diverse Actions Toward Climate Resilience
sections.content: Despite the climate crisis, investments in the renewable energy market are regaining momentum, bringing companies such as LS ELECTRIC and HD Hyundai Electric into the spotlight [9]. Korea South-East Power is moving forward with the construction of a large-scale 150 MW solar farm in Pyeongchang, while Seo-gu District in Daegu was selected for a support program to deploy renewable energy facilities across 47 sites [10, 12]. Furthermore, global brand Lululemon's supply chain achieved a 33% renewable electricity usage rate for 2025, and olive orchards in Afghanistan are offering new relief to farmers grappling with the climate crisis [11, 16].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing. Solidarity and decisive action to overcome this global crisis are more urgent than ever.
